audit.whatIsWrong: The entry treats Relentless Pursuit as a per-trade escape: "he can E-dash your Tongue Lash before the third stack", "his E resets deny the stack window in almost every real trade", "Lucian kites your stack-fishing with the E dash for free".
audit.why: Relentless Pursuit is 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s. It is one of the longest basic-ability cooldowns either champion owns — longer than Tahm Kench's own Abyssal Dive at rank 1 in effect, because Lucian only shortens it by landing Lightslinger attacks ("Lightslinger attacks reduce Relentless Pursuit's cooldown"). If he dodges one Tongue Lash with it and then misses his follow-up attacks, he has no exit for the better part of fifteen seconds. Telling the player the dash denies them "in almost every real trade" makes them play passive through the exact window that produces the 53.1% win rate.
audit.corrected: Relentless Pursuit is 16s at rank 1 and only ticks down faster when his Lightslinger attacks connect. One spent dash is a genuine 14-16 second window, not a beat.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lucian.json — Relentless Pursuit cooldown 16/15.5/15/14.5/14 and description

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere mentions that Piercing Light is cast on a target and travels through it.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Lucian shoots a bolt of piercing light through a target." The nominal range is only 500, but he can cast it on a minion and the bolt continues through to whatever is behind. For a melee tank the instinct is to stand behind the wave; against Lucian that turns the wave into his firing platform and hands him extra effective range. This is the most common way a Tahm Kench eats free poke in this lane and neither layer says a word about it.
audit.corrected: Piercing Light pierces through the target it is cast on. Standing behind minions does not shield you — it extends his reach by the width of the wave.

audit.whatIsWrong: The jungle section is generic and never explains why a gank on you is worse against Lucian than against other laners.
audit.why: Lightslinger: "When Lucian is healed or shielded by an ally, or when a nearby enemy Champion is immobilized, his next 2 basic attacks will deal bonus magic damage." Any CC the enemy jungler lands on Tahm Kench arms Lucian with two empowered attacks for free. The gank does more damage than the jungler's kit alone accounts for, which changes when you can afford to be caught out of position.
audit.corrected: Any hard CC landed on you near Lucian empowers his next two attacks through Lightslinger. Assume enemy jungle CC adds a chunk of Lucian damage on top of its own.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet-flagged: Tahm Kench wins 53.1% but content win[] gives Lucian 4 stages to Tahm Kench's 1. The full layer is worse — phases give Lucian 5 of 7, Skill 2, Tahm Kench 0.
audit.why: A chart where the winning champion owns zero stages cannot be right. The full layer also contradicts itself: phases[6].side is "Lucian" while its own why reads "Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power", and phases[5].side is "Skill" while its why reads "Heartsteel is your spike". Content win[6] already says Tahm Kench for the same stage the full layer gives to Lucian.
audit.corrected: Lucian owns levels 1-3 on range. Levels 4-5 are Skill, level 6 is Skill, and both item stages belong to Tahm Kench — which is what both layers' own prose already says.
sources: packet tahmkench.json — winRate 53.1, games 1548, defect "level chart contradicts data"; champ-data/tahmkench.full.js phases[5].why and phases[6].why

audit.whatIsWrong: content `mid`, `late` and whys[4] build the level-6 and late-game plan on "Abyssal Voyage".
audit.why: Tahm Kench has no Abyssal Voyage; W is Abyssal Dive and R is Devour. whys[4] uses it as the sole reason level 6 is contested, and `late` uses it for "you are never stuck on an island" — advice a player cannot act on.
audit.corrected: Level 6 gives Devour, a single-target removal. There is no global.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — W Abyssal Dive, R Devour

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2], wants.you[1], whys[6] and full tradeGood/dosFull all chain the Tongue Lash stun into Devour.
audit.why: Tongue Lash at three stacks stuns and consumes the stacks; Devour needs three stacks. One or the other. Against Lucian, Devour is strictly better — a stun he can walk out of the end of is not what stops a champion whose whole pattern is repositioning.
audit.corrected: Bank three stacks and spend them on Devour.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json — An Acquired Taste, Tongue Lash

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer names none of Lucian's abilities (packet-flagged) — it says "double-shot passive", "E dash", "Q and W" throughout.
audit.why: The full layer names Relentless Pursuit but nothing else. A player cannot track a cooldown they cannot name, and the abilities that matter here (Piercing Light's pierce, Ardent Blaze's mark-and-reveal, Lightslinger's post-cast double shot) each demand a different reaction.
audit.corrected: Lightslinger (P), Piercing Light (Q, 9s at rank 1), Ardent Blaze (W, 14s, marks and reveals), Relentless Pursuit (E, 16s), The Culling (R, 110s).

audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal for Lucian off Lightslinger, but that is a false positive from the phrase "When Lucian is healed or shielded by an ally" — the ability heals nothing itself. I did not add Grievous Wounds advice on that basis and the existing itemization correctly does not carry any.

edits.before: Lucian's passive double-shot and E dash make levels 1-3 genuinely painful — he pokes you with Q and W, then dashes back before your Tongue Lash can land the third stack, which means your stun is mostly decorative until he makes a mistake. Thick Skin is converting his poke passively, but he can keep you below the out-of-combat healing threshold by staying aggressive, so do not idle in auto range trying to stack An Acquired Taste. Throw Tongue Lash from maximum range to fish for the slow, accept that he will kite the third stack, and prioritize CS over kill pressure — every trade you survive is a trade he did not convert into a snowball.
edits.after: Lightslinger and Relentless Pursuit make levels 1-3 genuinely painful — he pokes with Piercing Light and Ardent Blaze, then dashes back before Tongue Lash lands a third stack. But Relentless Pursuit is 16s at rank 1 and only shortens when his Lightslinger attacks connect, so it is not the permanent escape it feels like. Note that Piercing Light is cast through a target: standing behind minions gives him a free platform instead of cover. Fish the slow from maximum range, prioritise CS over kill pressure, and remember every trade you survive is one he did not convert into a snowball.

edits.before: Level 6 opens Abyssal Voyage and gives you global threat, but Lucian can still E-dash your Tongue Lash and deny the 3-stack stun if you telegraph it. This is the Skill window: play around his E cooldown — the moment he burns it aggressively to trade, step up and force the Tongue Lash. If you land the slow and he has no dash available, that is your window to stack to three and punish with Devour. Your first tank item changes the math dramatically: Heartsteel or Sunfire means his double-shot poke no longer keeps you below Thick Skin's healing threshold, and one stun-into-Devour puts him on a clock he cannot survive.
edits.after: Level 6 opens Devour, not a global — a single-target removal that ends any fight Lucian has already committed to. This is the Skill window: play around Relentless Pursuit, 16s at rank 1 and only shortened by landed Lightslinger attacks. The moment he burns it to trade, step up and force Tongue Lash. If you land the slow with his dash gone, stack to three and spend them on Devour — never on the stun, which consumes the very same three. Your first tank item then changes the math: Heartsteel or Sunfire means Lightslinger no longer holds you under Thick Skin's healing threshold.

edits.before: At 2+ items you are what Lucian's kit is not built to answer — a near-unkillable frontliner whose Tongue Lash stun and Devour remove him from teamfights completely. He cannot burst through your grey-health conversion fast enough to escape a full 3-stack combo, and Thick Skin's activated shield absorbs the burst window he needs. Abyssal Voyage means you are never stuck on an island; roam, peel your carry, and let Lucian's laning lead evaporate against a target he cannot kill in three rotations.
edits.after: At 2+ items you are what Lucian's kit is not built to answer — a near-unkillable frontliner whose Devour removes him from teamfights completely. He cannot burst through your grey-health conversion fast enough to escape three stacks, and Thick Skin's activated shield absorbs the burst window he needs. One thing to keep respecting: Lightslinger empowers his next two attacks whenever a nearby enemy champion is immobilised, so enemy jungle CC landing on you hits harder than the jungler's own numbers suggest.

edits.after: He can Relentless Pursuit out of Tongue Lash and punish with a Lightslinger double-shot — but that dash is 16s at rank 1, not a per-trade tool.

edits.after: At level 3 he has the full poke loop and you still need three hits to arm Devour; Piercing Light cast through a minion makes the wave his platform, not your cover.

notes: The Relentless Pursuit correction is the one that matters here — the whole entry is written as though Lucian's dash is available every trade, which is what produces the impossible chart (a champion who wins 53.1% of games owning zero stages in the full layer). At 16s at rank 1 it is the longest routinely-tracked cooldown in the lane. Four chart edits are enum-style and will fail a strict +/-10% band: content win[3], content win[5], full phases[5].side, full phases[6].side. I did NOT propose a change to diff/diffRating here even though HARD 8.5/10 on a 53.1% lane looks wrong, because the labels are incoherent file-wide rather than wrong for this row specifically — Kennen at 53.41% is EVEN 6/10 while Fiora at 53.41% is HARD 8.5/10, and HARD appears anywhere from 48.97% to 54.75%. That is a systemic issue worth a separate pass over the whole table, not a per-matchup edit.
